rationale: This is essentially the archive's "Continuous Warehoused-Proceeds Deployment" with asset growth swapped for capex and the cash-deployment leg folded into the same rank — a cosmetic recombination of already-tested lagged-financing/cash-drawdown components rather than a new mechanism.

A 3-year smoothed conjunction of capex/assets and net external financing is little more than the published net-external-financing and investment anomalies averaged together, and it adds no economic content beyond the already-tested investment×financing bottleneck signals.

The intangible-expansion leg is a genuinely new component in this pair's archive and the equity-timing conjunction is economically coherent, though `intan` sparsity and its acquisition-driven overlap with goodwill growth warrant a coverage check.

Gross-PPE expansion conditioned on a short-versus-long debt maturity tilt introduces a financing-fragility dimension absent from prior proposals, and the expression's natural direction matches the stated negative sign, though the sign could plausibly reverse if maturity mismatch proxies for compensated risk.

The inventory-minus-PPE difference is not identifying what the hypothesis claims — firms with flat inventory but contracting PP&E score high on that leg — so the signal's long leg will mix genuine inventory gluts with capital-shrinking issuers, muddying interpretation of any result.

Re-expressing the archive's strongest components as within-firm time-series extremes is a substantive, diagnostically motivated change rather than a cosmetic variant, but the 5-period TS_RANK window is coarse and may induce heavy ties and unstable portfolio composition.
